The fixed circuit ran on garnet:mock with 100 shots. The counts were 00: 45 and 11: 55. All shots landed in 00 or 11, which is what a Bell pair should give. The job ID is 01a15f3c-7ed4-7705-a284-fa5605c69335. It was a mock job, so it cost no credits.

The original circuit had two bugs.

1. It used qubit QB25. Garnet has only 20 qubits (QB1 to QB20), so QB25 does not exist. I used QB2 as the partner instead. The architecture lists a calibrated cz coupler between QB2 and QB1.
2. It used a cx gate. cx is not a native IQM operation. Garnet accepts only prx, cz and measure. I built the CNOT from native gates: prx(angle=-pi/2, phase=pi/2) on QB2, which is Ry(-pi/2), then cz on QB1 and QB2, then prx(angle=pi/2, phase=pi/2) on QB2, which is Ry(pi/2).

I kept the first gate, prx(pi/2, pi/2) on QB1, which is Ry(pi/2) and puts QB1 in the |+> state. The circuit now produces (|00> + |11>)/sqrt(2) on QB1 and QB2. One measure instruction with key "m" reads both qubits. The fixed JSON is at /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_f3caa17a-2c4-72/bell_fixed.json.
